answer_1.quote: In this paper we are interested in summarizing longer narratives, i.e., screenplays ... We adapt general-purpose extractive summarization algorithms to identify informative scenes in screenplays and instill in them knowledge about narrative film structure.
answer_1.outputs: extractive scene summaries (selected scenes presented in original order)

answer_2.quote: We perform 10-fold cross-validation and evaluate model performance in terms of F1 score.

answer_4.quote: We also conducted a human evaluation experiment using the summaries created for 10 CSI episodes. ... We asked Amazon Mechanical Turk (AMT) workers to watch the video summaries for all systems and rank them from most to least informative. They were also presented with six questions relating to the aspects the summary was supposed to cover (e.g., Was the victim revealed in the summary? Do you know who the perpetrator was?).
answer_4.guideline: Crowdworkers were asked to rank the summaries by informativeness and answer yes/no/unsure to six aspect-related questions (victim, perpetrator, cause of death, evidence, motive, etc.).
